The '''cosmological fluid''' is a large-scale model of the [[Universe]]'s content.

It applies [[the Cosmological Principle]] and describes the Universe on large scales as a perfect fluid of '''energy density''' $\rho(t)$ and pressure $p(t)$.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Three species ==

{{#content:Q2620}}

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Species
! Content
! $p,\rho$
! $\rho,a$
|-
| Non-relativistic matter
| Galaxies, baryons, and cold dark matter
| $p_M=0$
| $\rho_M\propto a^{-3}$
|-
| Radiation
| Photons and ultra-relativistic particles 
| $p_R=\rho_R/3$
| $\rho_R\propto a^{-4}$
|-
| Vacuum energy
| 
| $p_\Lambda=-\rho_\Lambda$
| $\rho_\Lambda=\text{constant}$
|}

Since each component is independent,

$$
\rho_\text{total}=\sum \rho,\, 
p_\text{total}=\sum_x p.
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
